title: Hamming ball as the disjoint union of spheres
statement:
Let $u \in \alpha^n$ be a word of length $n$ over a finite alphabet $\alpha$, and let $r$ be a natural number. Then the Hamming ball of radius $r$ centred at $u$ is the disjoint union of the Hamming spheres of radii $0, 1, \dots, r$ centred at $u$:
\[
  B_r(u) = \bigsqcup_{k=0}^{r} S_k(u).
\]
hypotheses_covered: u is a word of length n over a finite alphabet α
r is a natural number (the radius)
replaced:
